result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers stick closely to the supplied facts and are honest that a sent reminder can't be recalled and that support can only read the log. A is a little stronger on what the freelancer can do after a reminder goes out (contact the client), but it adds an unsupported 'before launch' deadline to the policy question. B is easier to scan with its table and explicit 'Not mitigated' and 'Not yet decided' lists, so it suits engineers and the support lead slightly better. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): A is more scannable: its table makes the stop and cancel rules easy to check, though it never says what the freelancer can do once a reminder has gone. B covers that step (the freelancer contacts the client themselves) and links the log to the failure. However, B adds an unsupported 'before launch' deadline and says the policy needs an owner, while A adds an unsupported open item about a fix for the bank-transfer failure.
